Method of Attack: Information stealing by exfiltrating sensitive data from infected computers including browser profiles, cryptocurrency wallets, VPN client records, FTP programs, text documents, and Telegram sessions
Non-persistent malware that steals data in one go without persistence or spreading mechanisms
Uses short development cycles for continuous improvement
Data exfiltration via one large and obvious network transfer
Discoverer: Malwarebytes researchers (William Tsing, Vasilios Hioureas, Jérôme Segura)
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with installed browsers and applications such as Google Chrome, Exodus wallet, Ethereum keystore, ProtonVPN, Jaxx wallet, Liberty, NordVPN, Telegram, Jabber, TotalCommander, Ghisler
Attack Vector: Delivered individually to victims without spreading or reinfection
Distribution managed by cybercrime forum actors (Agressor for distribution, Overdot for sales and promotion, LordOdin for development)
Indicators of Compromise: Access to AppData folders including Chrome User Data (Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, History)
Document files (DOC, DOCZ, LOG, TXT) in default locations
One large network transfer of stolen data
